chunks.company: Bawadi Al Dain General Trading L.L.C
chunks.title: General trading from Dubai
chunks.text:
Bawadi Al Dain General Trading L.L.C is a Dubai limited liability company, licensed for general trading since 2020.
From its office in Al Garhoud, the company handles enquiries for natural gums, grain and livestock.
It is the commercial and export arm of Bawadi Al Dain Animal & Agricultural Production Co. Ltd. From its UAE hub, the company manages market access, international partnerships, logistics and the distribution of livestock, meat, feed, oils, grains and forest products from Sudan and from the group’s growing integrated operations in Mauritania, Senegal, Kenya, Somaliland and, through a joint venture, Iraq’s Kurdistan Region. Its UAE presence gives seamless connections to Gulf and global markets.
The Bawadi Al Dain group is a leading integrated agribusiness group specialising in livestock, meat processing, oilseeds, grains, vegetable oils and forest products. With a strong production base in Sudan, expanding integrated operations in Mauritania, Kenya and Somaliland, and a strategic commercial presence in the UAE, it delivers reliable, high-quality supply to regional and international buyers.
Following disruptions in Sudan, the group has pursued a deliberate regional expansion. In Mauritania this has taken the form of an integrated agricultural and livestock investment model covering livestock production, crop cultivation, feed production, slaughter facilities and related value-chain infrastructure. Through a joint venture, the group has also extended into Iraq’s Kurdistan Region.

chunks.company: Bawadi Al Dain General Trading L.L.C
chunks.title: Agricultural products
chunks.text:
Darfur and Kordofan remain cornerstone production regions for high-value crops including groundnuts, sesame, sunflower and complementary cash crops. The group complements these with pivot-irrigated fruit and vegetable production and extensive contract-farming programmes in Sudan.
In Mauritania, through its sister company Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL, the group is developing large-scale cultivation of forage crops and commercial agricultural commodities using both rain-fed and irrigated systems. Priority crops include peanuts, soybeans, watermelon seeds, sorghum and maize, and initial rain-fed farming has produced encouraging results. Downstream opportunities include edible oil production, peanut processing, animal-feed manufacturing and exports to regional markets including Algeria, Morocco, Senegal, Mali and Niger.
Similar agricultural development is planned under the group’s new companies in Kenya and Somaliland, to support integrated livestock and feed production.

chunks.company: Bawadi Al Dain General Trading L.L.C
chunks.title: Cattle and sheep
chunks.text:
Sudan is a major producer and exporter of live cattle and sheep. Bawadi Al Dain is among the leading suppliers to local and international markets, with a proven record of large-scale exports.
In Sudan the group keeps substantial standing herds and fattening capacity across East Darfur (Al Dain), Kordofan (Al Nuhood) and its Omdurman farms.
In Mauritania, land was acquired in 2023 in the Boghé/Aleg area of the Brakna Region for an integrated livestock quarantine and production facility under Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL, designed for up to 50,000 head of cattle, sheep and camels. Larger-scale facilities are also under development in Kenya and Somaliland, for local supply and exports to the GCC.

chunks.company: Bawadi Al Dain General Trading L.L.C
chunks.title: Camels
chunks.text:
One-humped camels are a key part of the group’s livestock portfolio, ranking immediately after cattle in export importance. They are highly valued across the Gulf and wider Saharan markets.
Bawadi Al Dain sources, aggregates and supplies camels from Sudan. In Mauritania, the Boghé/Aleg livestock facility includes camels within its overall capacity of up to 50,000 head of cattle, sheep and camels. Planned facilities in Kenya and Somaliland will further strengthen regional camel supply for GCC markets.

chunks.company: Bawadi Al Dain General Trading L.L.C
chunks.title: Forest products (gum arabic)
chunks.text:
Since 2001 the group has invested in Hashab ( Acacia senegal ) plantations and keeps substantial safety stocks of both Hashab and Talha ( Acacia seyal ) gum. It combines own-farm production, contract farming and large-scale procurement to ensure reliable volumes and consistent quality.
Its work includes R&D collaboration, tappers’ training and quality-improvement programmes across Sudan. The group also sources and trades gum arabic from Mauritania, Senegal, Kenya and Somalia, making it a dependable supplier to global industrial and food markets.

chunks.company: Bawadi Al Dain General Trading L.L.C
chunks.title: Grains and oilseeds
chunks.text:
The group holds a strong position in oilseed and grain supply from Sudan, with particular strength in peanuts, sesame, sunflower, gum arabic, hibiscus, baobab, chickpeas, pigeon peas and watermelon seeds. Peanut cake and sorghum feed are important export and local-market products.
Sudan produces over one million tons of peanuts a year. The group produces high-oil-content raw peanuts at scale and runs dedicated logistics, including its own fleet of trucks, from the production areas to its crushing and sorting facilities. Complementary sourcing from Chad, Mauritania, Kenya and Somalia supports volume and continuity for the UAE-based trading operations.

chunks.company: Bawadi Al Dain General Trading L.L.C
chunks.title: Meat processing
chunks.text:
Bawadi Al Dain operates and partners with slaughter and meat-processing facilities that meet international standards for export and domestic markets. Its focus is a value-added chain for cattle, sheep and goats that complies with global quality, food-safety and Halal requirements.
In Sudan, the Al-Kadaro Meat Processing Complex provides significant capacity and holds ISO, HACCP and Halal certification.
In Mauritania, sister company Mauritania Meat Company (MMC) has been set up to operate slaughter facilities for local meat sales, for regional exports to neighbouring countries including Algeria, Morocco, Senegal, Mali and Niger, and for global markets. It is part of the wider integrated investment model, which also includes leather-processing facilities.
In Kenya, Al-Rahma for Development and Animal & Agricultural Production Co. is developing a slaughterhouse alongside its livestock facility, mainly for local sales and exports to the GCC. A similar integrated livestock and slaughterhouse project is planned in Somaliland, for local sales and GCC exports.

(Production in Sudan)
Bawadi Al Dain Animal & Agricultural Production Co. Ltd Registered in Sudan
Bawadi Al Dain Animal & Agricultural Production Co. Ltd is a separately registered company in Sudan. Its core business is agriculture, oils and livestock production, in production regions that include Darfur and Kordofan.
Its activities support the livelihoods of people in these production areas. It also helps to form farmers’ unions, so that small farmers share in the benefit and can cope with costs and price fluctuations.

chunks.text:
(Agricultural Products)
Darfur, one of the company’s production regions, is a major agricultural region of Sudan. Its cash crops matter to the national economy and are a source of livelihood for families across the region.
- Groundnuts Darfur regularly provides two-thirds of Sudan’s national groundnut harvest.
- Gum arabic An important traditional source of supply.
- Oranges Jebel Marra is a main growing area, supplying central Sudan and all of Darfur.
- Sesame A high-value export crop for Sudan.

chunks.title: Key projects in Sudan
chunks.text:
Rubu Kordofan Project:
(Al-Nahud, West Kordofan · 176 acres)
A centre for fattening calves and for breeding sheep and improving their strains, with farms on both sides growing beans, sesame and citrus fruits.
Qarnaya Agricultural Project:
(North of Ad-Daein, East Darfur · 45 km²)
A major crossroads for livestock from across Darfur. Its three water stations are an important reserve for the people of the region. Improved seeds of peanuts, sesame, hibiscus, corn and millet are developed here; sunflower was grown successfully, and horticultural crops were planted for the first time to produce improved fruit.

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: Agriculture and livestock in Mauritania
chunks.text:
(About Us)
Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale is a Mauritanian limited liability company, established in Nouakchott in 2023.
Its programme covers forage, livestock breeding and fattening, animal feed, veterinary care, slaughtering and dairy, developed in stages.
Arrahma is the Mauritanian company of the Bawadi Al Dain group. Its integrated model covers livestock production, crop cultivation, feed production, slaughter facilities and related value-chain infrastructure.

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: Built on more than 35 years of experience
chunks.text:
(Who We Are)
Our story began with the founding of Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale in Mauritania, where a dream became reality through vision, hard work and the challenge to excel. We started with small, deliberate steps towards our goals, and these soon became steady progress and rapid implementation.
The story is embodied in our founder, the businessman Muhammad Hamid Abkar, who holds the majority of the company’s shares with his family.

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: Muhammad Hamid Abkar
chunks.text:
(Founder and Chairman of the Board)
One of Sudan’s leading businessmen in agriculture, livestock production and related manufacturing. Over a career of more than 35 years he has built a large, well-established business with a direct impact on the development of agriculture and livestock in Sudan.

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: His achievements in Sudan
chunks.text:
- Buying, gathering, raising and fattening livestock and supplying it to large companies and institutions, including Alategahat Almtadeda Co. Ltd, a Sudanese government company and a leading exporter of meat and livestock to Egypt, whose exports have passed 500,000 head in recent years
- Thousands of acres of crops in rain-fed areas such as Wadi Al-Daein, Darfur, Kordofan and Al-Jazira, and in irrigated areas: peanuts, cotton and forage crops
- A farm for the genetic improvement of local cattle through artificial insemination with frozen semen imported from abroad
- Large farms for cattle, sheep and camels in Al-Nahud, Darfur and Omdurman
- Peanut collection and sorting centres that export first-grade peanuts, and two oil mills, in Al-Obeid and in Al-Baqir near Khartoum, whose oil is exported and whose cake is sold at home and abroad
- Social and humanitarian work in his home region, through partnerships with small herders and support for building schools and hospitals

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: Dr Saad Alhayani
chunks.text:
(Our technical team)
Head of the technical team
The company relies on a group of technical experts and consultants who cover all its production activities. It is led by Dr Saad Alhayani, who has more than 40 years of experience in agriculture and livestock in countries including Egypt, Sudan, Chad and Mauritania, and has set up dozens of agricultural and livestock projects over the past four decades. He is supported by experienced agricultural, veterinary and executive teams.

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: Why the company chose Mauritania
chunks.text:
(Why Mauritania)
- Vast, good land, with water from rivers, rainfall and renewable groundwater
- More than 25 million head of livestock: cattle, sheep, goats and camels
- No farm in the country yet raises and fattens livestock on a large scale
- Neighbouring countries that import live animals and meat
- Investment-friendly laws, and a real will among senior officials to encourage investment
- A relatively mild climate in summer and winter
As set out in the company’s profile.

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: Our vision
chunks.text:
(Vision and Values)
Arrahma’s vision in Mauritania is strategic: to lay the first stone in renewing and developing agriculture and livestock production, in cooperation with the competent authorities. With a firm commitment to excellence, sustainability and innovation, the company aims to be a leading force in the country’s agriculture and livestock sector.
It pursues this through several large-scale projects in crop and livestock production, feed manufacturing, slaughterhouses for red meat, and milk and dairy products, to meet local and international needs.

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: Five production sites across Mauritania
chunks.text:
(Our Goals)
The company plans five production sites in different regions of Mauritania over five to eight years. Each site is designed for:

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: Short-term goals
chunks.text:
- 20 irrigation pivots of 50 hectares each, for 1,000 to 1,100 hectares of forage crops
- A total mixed ration (TMR) feed factory of 40 tonnes an hour, enough for one site at full fattening capacity: a blend of concentrates, roughage, salts and vitamins prepared to each animal’s needs
- A full veterinary laboratory at each site, working with the Directorate of Veterinary Services to monitor animal health, vaccination and disease
- An automated slaughterhouse for 50 cattle and 200 sheep an hour and 50 camels a day, with cutting, deboning and processing halls and cold rooms
- Exports of live animals and red meat, raised to international quality, to importing Arab and African countries

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: Long-term goals
chunks.text:
- Meat shops in Mauritania built to world standards of quality, hygiene and cold storage
- Exports of portioned, vacuum-packed meat, with premium cuts separated from standard cuts
- A genetic improvement farm for local cattle, using imported frozen semen from sires of proven high-yielding lines
- A dairy farm of improved, high-yielding cows suited to Mauritania
- A dairy factory for long-life milk (six-month shelf life), cheeses, yoghurt and other dairy products
- A large agro-industrial complex serving Mauritania and Africa, with products certified to international standards such as ISO and HACCP

chunks.company: Arrahma pour la Production Agricole et Animale – SARL
chunks.title: The second site: Hodh Ech Chargui
chunks.text:
On about 1,000 hectares acquired with local breeders, the second strategic quarantine site will have pens for raising and fattening cattle, sheep and camels. Land levelling, fencing and site planning are under way.
Plans include developing rangeland on rain-fed land with drought- and salt-tolerant forage seed, wells to use groundwater in the dry season, and ponds that store rainwater for supplementary irrigation.
What the project is expected to bring:
- Work for hundreds of people: farm and livestock workers, administrators and technicians
- Dozens of machines, from tractors and loaders to seeders, harvesters and balers, with drivers, technicians and mechanics
- A more active livestock market in the region
- Veterinary care and technical advice for local breeders
- Modern forage farming that raises yields and improves animal health and growth
- An incentive for breeders to raise more, healthier animals to supply the site, which will raise and fatten tens of thousands of head a year
Goals and plans as reported by the company.
